assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reframed how technology and trade reshape labour demand, wage inequality and local labour markets. The task-based approach and the evidence on import-competition shocks changed academic research and public debate. Evidence quality is high and it speaks to central questions of distribution and adjustment.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the task framework and the China-shock work. Hanson is the trade-side co-originator of the local labour-market shock evidence. Katz anchors the earlier supply-demand (skill-biased change) literature. Dorn is a key co-author of the China-shock papers but is left out of this three-name set, and the choice among the four is genuinely contestable.
assessment.maturity: Foundational papers are 15 to 30 years old, with a large replication and extension literature. Some later work has refined or qualified the original estimates, which indicates the field has matured.
uncertainties: Whether the committee treats the skill-bias and task contributions and the trade-shock contributions as one discovery or as two.
Which three of four names best capture the credit.
Debate over the size and persistence of the China-shock effects and over the task framework's empirical content.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-firm trade models changed how the field thinks about selection, reallocation and the gains from trade. They became the workhorse of modern trade theory and empirics, moving analysis from industries to firms. The contribution is deep, widely taught and used for policy evaluation.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the clear originating model. Helpman, with Melitz and Yeaple, extended it to exporting versus FDI choices and shaped the broader research agenda. Redding's quantitative and spatial extensions are important but more derivative of the core discovery. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, who provide key related empirical and quantitative contributions, are not on this ballot entry.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of confirmation and extension, with extensive empirical validation using firm-level data.
uncertainties: Credit relative to the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum line of work, which is not credited here.
Overlap with the Helpman-Grossman trade-politics entry, which also credits Helpman.
Debate over whether gains-from-trade implications depend on specific distributional assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework underpin modern monetary policy analysis in central banks and academia. The work includes microfounded price-setting, the Taylor rule and the New Keynesian Phillips curve, and it guides practical policy design. Its influence on actual institutions and policy practice is very large.
assessment.attribution: The credit is highly distributed across many contributors, including Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and Gertler. Any three-person set leaves out important contributors, and the committee must decide whether to honour the theory (Woodford, Gali), the policy rule (Taylor) or the pricing model (Calvo). Fischer and Phelps are also relevant to the staggered-contracts lineage.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use and refinement. The framework was stress-tested by the financial crisis and the post-2021 inflation, and it has survived with modifications.
uncertainties: Large and contestable attribution problem with eight credited names.
Lingering criticism of the framework's performance after the financial crisis and during the inflation surge.
Overlap with heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian work and the Gertler credit-cycle entries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Created a systematic, empirically testable economics of constitutions, electoral rules, state capacity and fiscal policy. This brought formal political economics into mainstream applied work and opened a major field on institutions and development. The contribution is important, with clear conceptual and empirical content.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the central pair through their joint research program and synthesising books. Besley's work on state capacity, accountability and political agency, with Persson and others, is close in scope. The trio is a coherent and widely recognised grouping.
assessment.maturity: A mature literature spanning roughly 30 years. It has been replicated and extended with credible identification in some strands.
uncertainties: Some constitutional and cross-country empirical results rest on weaker identification.
Overlap with the institutions and development literature already recognised by earlier prizes.
Persson's role on the committee list is not treated as evidence of merit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Legal origins and investor protection reshaped comparative financial and institutional economics. The work shifted attention to how legal institutions shape financial development and governance. It was highly influential, though it has been challenged and refined.
assessment.attribution: La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny are the original quartet, and the prize allows at most three. Shleifer is the intellectual leader across several adjacent areas. The choice of three leaves out Vishny, which is a real attribution problem.
assessment.maturity: Foundational papers date from the late 1990s. There has been long debate over the legal-origins thesis, including critiques of measurement and causal interpretation.
uncertainties: Substantial empirical and conceptual criticism of the legal-origins hypothesis.
Limited scope for exclusion of Vishny among the four originators.
Reputational and conduct controversies around one credited researcher that the committee might weigh, though they are not adjudicated here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression is a core statistical tool that lets researchers study the whole conditional distribution rather than just the mean. It is used across labour, inequality, finance and many other fields. Its methodological reach is wide and durable.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett (1978) introduced the estimator, and Koenker developed the theory, computation and applications over decades. Chernozhukov's contributions to inference and instrumental and censored quantile methods are important, but his largest contributions are better matched to other methodological entries.
assessment.maturity: More than 45 years of use and confirmation, so timing is not a concern.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as a primarily statistical contribution relative to its economic content.
Whether Chernozhukov should be included given his other credited work.
Substantial overlap with the statistics literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data changed measurement of intergenerational mobility and of place effects on opportunity. The work combines large-scale data with credible quasi-experimental designs and has high policy relevance. It created new standards for empirical measurement in public and labour economics.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear leader of the program. Hendren and Friedman are key collaborators on neighbourhood effects and mobility. Katz contributed to the Moving to Opportunity reanalysis. The group shares credit, and some distinctive contributions belong to a large co-author team.
assessment.maturity: Mostly 2014 onward. Impact is already very large, but some long-run replication, external validity and interpretation questions are still open.
uncertainties: Relatively recent work, with some findings still under scrutiny.
Scope and credit overlap with the optimal-taxation entry that also credits Chetty.
Whether the committee prefers measurement advances or underlying methodology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learning methods for causal inference, including debiased machine learning, causal forests and heterogeneous treatment effects, extend the credibility toolkit to high-dimensional data. They are widely adopted in applied work and in the technology sector. The contribution is methodologically substantial and has broad application.
assessment.attribution: Chernozhukov, with co-authors, developed double or debiased machine learning. Athey and Wager developed causal forests, and Athey also led the broader program connecting machine learning and economics. Wager is more of a statistician and a later-career contributor. Several important co-authors, such as Imbens, Belloni and Newey, are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: The core papers date from about 2015 to 2018. Adoption is rapid, but the long-run test of influence is still developing.
uncertainties: Relatively early for a prize.
Complex attribution given other key contributors, including some outside this ballot entry.
Chernozhukov is also credited on the quantile-regression entry.
